liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Eyes Of The World** (3 reviews): Eyes is praised as a return to a mellower, 1970s-style version; Eyes was outstanding, part of a 1990 revival of the song credited to the 3/29 show [20][22][24]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Bertha is described as lightning fast and hot, opening the show [22]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Bertha and Jack Straw are hot, followed by Phil's classic speech, making the opening tracks essential [24]
- **Picasso Moon** (1 review): Picasso Moon is called underrated, with Jerry sounding inspired [29]
- **Standing On The Moon** (1 review): Reviewer recalls Standing on the Moon as one of the better versions they saw [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1990-06-10.schoeps.unknown.457.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): source not stated; 22 songs; 187 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1990-06-10.142579.FOB.Schoeps.Weber-Small.Mattes.Miler.Noel.t-flac1648**: source not stated; 22 songs; 159 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1990-06-10.schoeps.wklitz.97059.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 159 min; rated 2/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1990-06-10.168425.3xnakcm300.ont.flac1644**: source not stated; 21 songs; 160 min [4]
- **gd1990-06-10.152180.nakcp702.flac2496**: source not stated; 21 songs; 163 min [5]. Said about its sound: Right channel dropped out several times due to cabling; fixed by copying the left channel, making those moments mono; Both channels cut for about 20 seconds at the end of the NFA chant; the silence was edited out [5]
- **gd90-06-10.sbd-matrix.miller-ladner.6937.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 152 min; rated 4.25/5 by 44 [7]. Said about its sound: Matrix recording has remarkable clarity, with just enough audience noise to convey the party atmosphere; Sound quality is excellent; the rest of the performance is average to good; Very clean sound, avoiding the harshness of some other shows, paired with tight playing [19][24][25]

## Around the show

- Phil's "bullshit lie" remark is remembered as a classic moment; the reviewer says Cal Expo was one of a kind [19]
- Sunday afternoon start rather than evening; small, fast hot-air-balloon-like objects floated over Cal Expo during the show [27]
- Rumors of Phil leaving the band circulated heavily in Oregon before summer tour; small balloons with dancing-bear pictures passed over [28]
- Phil squashed the rumors of his leaving and then played powerfully all night [29]
- Eileen Law and the writer told Phil before the show about many calls on the quitting rumor; he promised to end it [30]
- Phil's announcement came after Jack Straw; the taper drove from San Luis Obispo County and met Bear Owsley in the tapers section [4]
- Reviewer ranks this and the 9th as the best soundboard/matrix recordings they have heard [19]
- Called possibly the best show of the Cal Expo, Shoreline and Eugene run, and among the summer's best [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1990-06-10.schoeps.unknown.457.sbefail.shnf**: taped by Unknown; transferred by unknown; source: daud>>sch mk4>>D>>CD [1]
- **gd1990-06-10.142579.FOB.Schoeps.Weber-Small.Mattes.Miler.Noel.t-flac1648**: taped by Sean Weber-Small; transferred by Joe Noel and Ted Mattes and Charlie Miller; source: flac16/48kHz ;Sean Weber-Small (FOB) Recording: Schoeps CMC4 MK2 > Oade Power Supply > DAT 48k (Panasonic SV-250). Mics spaced 8' w/ mic stands @ 5' 11";… [2]
- **gd1990-06-10.schoeps.wklitz.97059.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Keith Litzenberger; transferred by Keith Litzenberger; source: Schoeps Omni Spaced 27'>Oade?>Technics SV-MD1 in Taper's Section DAT MASTER>Tascam DA-30MKII>Sound Devices 702>Soundforge 9>CDWAV>FLAC (It's likely that my DAT… [3]. Also: DAT likely patched through the lead deck's analog output, since mics weren't the taper's and the Technics lacks digital in; Second set was on a 90-minute DAT; tapes swapped before the encore, so some audience chant is missing [3]
- **gd1990-06-10.168425.3xnakcm300.ont.flac1644**: taped by OldNeumanntapr; transferred by OldNeumanntapr; source: OTS; Nakamichi CM-300s x3; Two CP-4 Shotgun Capsules + One CP-3 Super Omni Mixed With Radio Shack Mixer >Aiwa HD-X1 DAT >Sony WM-D6C (Patch) [TDK MA110s] [4]. Also: Sony WM-D6C patched into a friend John's Nakamichi CM300x3 rig, later bought by the taper [4]
- **gd1990-06-10.152180.nakcp702.flac2496**: source: FOB Nakamichi CP-702 omni capsules, 12' spread > custom pre-amp/power supply > Dbx Type II noise reduction encoder > Sony TC-D5 cassette [5]. Also: Master cassette from a setup feeding multiple chained recorders, mastered with Waves L3 Ultramaximizer [5]
- **gd90-06-10.sbd-matrix.miller-ladner.6937.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD/Matrix > DAT > CDR > WAV > SHN [7]. Also: A good Schoeps FOB recording of this show is also in circulation [20]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead BGP Laminate, Cal Expo Amphitheatre](https://www.dead.net/archives/1990/artwork/bgp-laminate-cal-expo-amphitheatre) [32]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Cal Expo Amphitheatre - June 10, 1990](https://www.dead.net/show/june-10-1990) [33]

DAT master from Ted Mattes, recorded by Sean Weber-Small using Ted's rig
DAT likely patched through the lead deck's analog output, since mics weren't the taper's and the Technics lacks digital in
Second set was on a 90-minute DAT; tapes swapped before the encore, so some audience chant is missing
Phil's announcement came after Jack Straw; the taper drove from San Luis Obispo County and met Bear Owsley in the tapers section
Sony WM-D6C patched into a friend John's Nakamichi CM300x3 rig, later bought by the taper
Right channel dropped out several times due to cabling; fixed by copying the left channel, making those moments mono
Both channels cut for about 20 seconds at the end of the NFA chant; the silence was edited out
Master cassette from a setup feeding multiple chained recorders, mastered with Waves L3 Ultramaximizer
